Name: Gaslighting
Definition: This is a type of psychological manipulation in which a person sows seeds of doubt in another person's mind, making them question their own perceptions and memories. In the context of dating, a partner may use gaslighting to make the other person feel crazy or confused, which can be a form of emotional abuse.

Definition: This is a type of bonding that can occur in abusive relationships, in which a person becomes emotionally attached to their abuser as a result of the intense emotional experiences they share. Trauma bonding can make it difficult for a person to leave an abusive relationship, even when they know it is not healthy for them.

Name: Instilling phobias
Definition: According to Lifton, phobia indoctrination involves creating an intense fear or anxiety around a particular idea, belief, or action. This fear is often reinforced through repeated exposure to certain stimuli or events, and can become so powerful that it overwhelms the individual's ability to think rationally or make decisions independently. In the context of relationships, phobia indoctrination might be used by an abusive partner to control their partner's behavior.

Name: Cognitive dissonance
Cleanup note: 3 Oct 2026: removed double asterisks (bold markup) from title
Definition: Cognitive dissonance is a state of psychological discomfort that arises when a person's beliefs or values are in conflict with their actions. In abusive relationships, victims may experience cognitive dissonance because they love their partner but also know that their behavior is harmful.

Name: Attachment theory
Definition: How early childhood experiences with caregivers can shape a person's attachment style in adult relationships. In pathological love relationships, the victim may have an anxious attachment style, which makes them clingy and insecure in relationships.

Name: Learned helplessness
Definition: Learned helplessness is a mental state where a person feels powerless to change their situation, even when they have the ability to do so. Victims of abuse may develop learned helplessness because they feel trapped in their relationship and don't see a way out.

Name: Cycle of abuse
Definition: Predictable rotation of abusive behavior into honeymoon phase, buildup (tension) phase, explosion, rationalization
